title: Local Broadband Gigahertz Spectroscopy via SQUID-on-Tip DC Readout
authors: Senne Vervoort, Lukas Nulens, Julia Baumgarten, Daan B. Boltje, Jessalyn DeVine, Alejandro V. Silhanek, Joris Van de Vondel, Kaveh Lahabi
abstract: Superconducting microwave circuits are shaped by their local electromagnetic environment, yet standard microwave measurements do not resolve the local fields and device features that govern their behavior. Here, we combine microwave spectroscopy, nanoscale magnetic sensing, and topographic imaging in a single tapping-mode SQUID-on-tip microscope. The nonlinear Josephson response converts local GHz excitations into Shapiro steps, enabling quantitative measurements of microwave frequency signals and their excitation strength using only DC readout. Applied to a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator, local spectroscopy reproduces the power-dependent resonance and nonlinear bifurcation observed in microwave transmission measurements. Spatially resolved measurements map the microwave response while simultaneously recording topography and static magnetic features, including vortices and Meissner screening currents. Electromagnetic simulations reveal how coupling through the superconducting probe leads limits spatial resolution and guides localized detector designs. Together, these capabilities establish a platform for correlating microwave circuit dynamics with the local structural and magnetic environment of superconducting devices.
summary: This work introduces a novel SQUID-on-tip microscope that integrates microwave spectroscopy, magnetic sensing, and topography. By converting local GHz microwave signals into measurable DC Shapiro steps, the technique allows for unprecedented, spatially resolved mapping of microwave fields within superconducting circuits. This capability is vital for correlating circuit dynamics with the local structural and magnetic environment of superconducting devices.
main_problem: Standard microwave measurements fail to resolve the local electromagnetic environment and device features governing superconducting microwave circuits.
main_result: The SQUID-on-tip setup successfully reproduces power-dependent resonance and allows for simultaneous, spatially resolved mapping of microwave fields, topography, and static magnetic fields.
method: The technique combines microwave spectroscopy, nanoscale magnetic sensing, and topography using a tapping-mode SQUID-on-tip microscope.
model_or_system: The platform uses a SQUID coupled to a superconducting coplanar waveguide (CPW) resonator, exploiting the nonlinear Josephson response to convert local GHz excitations into measurable DC Shapiro steps.
key_observables: Shapiro steps, critical current suppression ($\Delta I_c$), local microwave field amplitude ($	ext{B}_{\mu	ext{w}}$), and topography.
important_parameters: Intrinsic Josephson Timescale ($f_c = 96.2$ GHz); spatial resolution limited by probe geometry.
main_assumptions: The SQUID response depends only on the normal component of the magnetic field; spatial resolution is limited by the superconducting probe leads.
figures_summary: Figures show schematics of the SQUID probe, $I-V$ curves demonstrating Shapiro steps, spatial maps of $\Delta I_c$ confirming field localization, and height dependence of the magnetic field.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the combined SQUID-on-tip platform, demonstrates its ability to measure microwave resonance locally, and uses simulations to model the field mapping and spatial resolution limits.
why_interesting: The ability to map local microwave fields with high spatial resolution provides a powerful tool for understanding dissipation and non-linear dynamics in superconducting circuits, which is crucial for quantum device engineering.
